science.title: Myristic acid promotes in vitro maturation and developmental competence of porcine oocytes
science.description: The present study examined how antral follicle size influences oocyte meiotic maturation and developmental competence from a metabolic perspective and explored strategies to improve the meiotic maturation and quality of oocytes derived from small antral follicles. Untargeted metabolomics revealed dynamic metabolic changes during porcine antral follicle development, with increased fatty acid synthesis and enhanced activities of related enzymes in oocytes from larger follicles. In vitro, myristic acid (MA) improved meiotic maturation (polar body extrusion, spindle morphology, chromosome dynamics) and survival of oocytes from small follicles by reducing Annexin V expression and ROS levels. MA also enhanced their developmental competence after parthenogenetic activation. Molecular and cytochemical analyses showed that MA altered the transcriptional profile, increased lipid storage, and boosted mitochondrial number and function. Finally, MA upregulated SIRT1, activated PPARα, and increased CPT2 expression, suggesting a potential mechanism underlying its effects on these oocytes.

science.title: Comparative analysis of gate-dielectric effects on the analog and linearity performance of MoS2-, MoSe2-, and WS2-based FETs
science.description: This work investigates the influence of gate dielectric engineering on the analog, RF, and linearity performance of transition metal dichalcogenide field-effect transistors (TMD-FETs). A self-consistent non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF)-based simulation framework is employed to analyze MoS2-, MoSe2-, and WS₂-based FETs integrated with different high-k gate dielectrics. The impact of dielectric materials on electrostatic integrity, carrier transport, transistor efficiency (gm/ID), quality factor (Q-factor), and RF linearity metrics is systematically examined. Key device parameters including ON current (ION), OFF current (IOFF), current ON/OFF ratio (ION/IOFF), subthreshold swing (SS), transconductance (gm), second-order transconductance (gm2), and third-order transconductance (gm3) are evaluated. The results demonstrate that high-k dielectrics significantly enhance gate electrostatic control, resulting in improved ON-state current, reduced SS, enhanced gm/ID efficiency, and superior Q-factor characteristics. Furthermore, the use of high-k dielectrics shifts the peaks of gm2 and gm3 toward lower gate voltages, indicating improved low-voltage RF linearity behavior. Among the investigated materials, WS₂-based FETs exhibit superior transconductance and RF performance characteristics, while MoS2-based devices provide an excellent trade-off between power efficiency, nonlinear distortion behavior, and analog/RF characteristics. The findings offer essential insights for optimizing dielectric–channel combinations in next-generation low-power, high-linearity, and RF-oriented nanoelectronic devices.

science.title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation promotes arthritis resolution by modulating joint cell phenotype involving E-series resolvins
science.description: The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. Non-classical monocytes and VCAM-1+ synovial fibroblasts were lower at peak arthritis while pro-resolution MerTK+CD206+ macrophages were increased at resolution onset. Lipid mediator profiling of arthritic paws identified a distinct repertoire of molecules in ω3-fed mice, with elevated EPA-derived resolvin E2 (RvE2) and RvE4, compared with increased TXB2 and PGF2α with a normal diet. Pharmacological treatment of mice with RvE2 and RvE4 concomitant with arthritis induction, attenuated arthritis and increased MerTK+CD206+ macrophages in arthritic joints. Synovial explant treatment revealed reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and enzyme release including IL-6, CCL2 and MMP-9. In arthritic patient blood, RvE2 and RvE4 (100 nM) lowered monocyte ICAM-1 expression. Collectively, these data identify cellular and molecular determinants of an ω3 diet in pre-clinical and human settings, highlighting therapeutic potential.
